sammendrag: [The ‘Strategic review of effective re-engagement models for disengaged learners’] was commissioned by Skills Victoria on behalf of the Victorian Skills Commission’s Access and Equity Committee and prepared by the Centre for Research on Education Systems (CRES), University of Melbourne. The review is undertaken in the context of national attainment targets set by Australian governments to halve the proportion of Australian adults without qualifications at Certificate III level or above, and to increase the percentage of young people who complete Year 12 or its equivalent to 90 per cent. [These groups] are at a significant disadvantage in the labour market, increased risk of becoming marginalized from it and are more likely to experience social exclusion. The review identified practices and strategies that work to help improve levels of educational participation and attainment of low skill and disengaged adult learners, focusing on 15- to 64-year-olds who have not attained initial qualifications (Year 12 or equivalent) and are unemployed, not in the labour force or in low-skill jobs. This report of the findings profiles the characteristics of low skilled, working age Victorians who have disengaged from education and training and documents effective practices and programs to re-engage them. The report also provides advice on programmatic costs, potential funding models and approaches to program evaluation. It draws on Australian and international literature and advice gathered through targeted stakeholder consultations, including on effective practice in Victoria.
tittel: Strategic review of effective re-engagement models for disengaged learners
